It addresses the limitations of the Uncertainty Theorem in signal processing, which states that a function cannot be simultaneously limited in both space and frequency domains [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the evidence addresses the limitations of the Uncertainty Theorem in signal processing, specifically that a function cannot be simultaneously limited in both space and frequency domains. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Unfortunately these two constraints can never be met exactly, since the Uncertainty Theorem states that a spatially limited function has an infinite extent in the frequency domain, and vice versa.' It further explains that the POCS method is used to approximate these conflicting constraints. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

The method computes a discrete 3D resampling filter $h(x,y,z)$ through an iterative projection process that alternates between spatial and frequency domain constraints [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method computes a discrete 3D resampling filter $h(x,y,z)$ through an iterative projection process alternating between spatial and frequency domain constraints. The evidence explicitly describes the Projection on Convex Sets (POCS) method, which starts with a function in the frequency domain, transforms it to the spatial domain to apply a spatial constraint (chopping tails), transforms it back to the frequency domain to apply a frequency constraint (chopping tails), and repeats this iteration. This matches the description in the claim exactly.
